increase the threat for flash flooding impacts on top of flooded

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Otero County in south central New Mexico...

* Until 1045 PM MDT.

heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain

to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 8:04PM MST until October 25 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall on Wednesday and
Thursday continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST Saturday Night /100 AM MDT Sunday/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is imminent or
occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 750 PM MST /850 PM MDT/, Elevated flow continues near Winslow
to Leupp. Elevated flow is forecast to continue through at least
Saturday evening.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 7:00pm MST /8:00pm MDT/ the stage was 18.06 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest near 18 feet is expected at 8:00pm MST /9:00pm
MDT/ Friday.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Leupp, Birdsprings, Bushman Acres, Homolovi Ruins State Park.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of rivers are unstable and
unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous. Do not attempt to cross
flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

* IMPACTS...At 14.5 feet, Water has reached the foundations of some
homes in the San Juan River Ranch northeast of Pagosa Springs.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.

at 11:00 PM MDT Thursday was 13.6 feet.

then fall below flood stage tomorrow evening to 8.0 feet Saturday

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 23 at 11:43PM EDT until October 24 at 12:15AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Straits of Florida from Craig Key to Halfmoon Shoal 20 to 60 nm
out...

* Until 1215 AM EDT.

* At 1143 PM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located 27 nm southwest
of Marathon Humps, moving southwest at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater and small hail.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.
